options.text: No — it's a compile-time macro available in <script setup>

questions.explanation: defineProps (like defineEmits and defineModel) is a compile-time macro handled by the SFC compiler — you use it without importing it.

questions.prompt: How do you give type-based props default values?

options.text: You can't have defaults with the type-based form

questions.explanation: The withDefaults helper adds default values to type-based props: withDefaults(defineProps<T>(), { size: 'md' }).

questions.prompt: Can a child component change the value of a prop it receives?

options.text: No — props are read-only; emit an event or copy to local state to change data
Only if the prop is a number

questions.explanation: Props follow one-way data flow and are read-only in the child. To change parent-owned data, emit an event; for an editable value, copy the prop into local state.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between likes="42" and :likes="42" on a component?

options.text: likes="42" passes the string "42"; :likes="42" binds the expression, passing the number 42

questions.explanation: A plain attribute passes a literal string; v-bind (:) evaluates the expression, so :likes="42" passes the number 42.

questions.prompt: Props flow in ______ direction(s) — parent to child — and are read-only in the child. (a number word)
questions.explanation: This is one-way data flow: data flows one direction, down from parent to child, and props are read-only.

questions.prompt: A child needs an editable value seeded from a prop. What's the correct approach?

options.text: Copy the prop into a local ref and edit that

questions.explanation: Since props are read-only, copy the prop into a local ref for the child to edit (and use a watcher if it must re-sync when the prop changes).
